summary.headline: Anupam Rasayan Q2 FY27 consolidated EBITDA rose 41% YoY to ₹202 crore (≈25% margin) after completing BLISS-GBS acquisition on 28 Sept 2026.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income rose 11% YoY to ₹821 crore in Q2 FY27 and H1 total income rose 21% to ₹1,489 crore. EBITDA margin expanded to about 25% in Q2 versus 19% a year earlier, driven by performance materials and product mix. Standalone revenue fell YoY because Q2 FY26 included a one-time sale of about ₹180 crore. BLISS-GBS was consolidated for only three days in the quarter, and management guided H2 consolidated revenue to ₹2,400-2,500 crore.

financial_highlights.change: vs full-year FY26 operating cash flow of ₹334 crore

segments.name: Life science related specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: Contributed 42% of Q2 FY27 revenue and 41% of H1 FY27 revenue.

segments.name: Performance materials
segments.commentary: Contributed 28% of Q2 FY27 revenue and 29% of H1 FY27; management said it was the main driver of the margin improvement.

segments.name: Other fluorinated products
segments.commentary: Contributed 29% of Q2 FY27 revenue and 28% of H1 FY27 revenue.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 consolidated revenue expected at about ₹2,400-2,500 crore, with BLISS-GBS and J-Hawk included for full periods; annualised run-rate of about ₹4,800-5,000 crore cited.
Standalone order book (LOIs and long-term contracts) about ₹1,750 crore per management; standalone revenue from it expected at roughly 1.8-2x last year's ~₹350 crore this year.
Organic growth target of about 20-25% over the near-term 3-5 year period.
BLISS-GBS steady-state EBITDA margin guided at 22-24%, in line with the group's consolidated margin guidance.
Management expects revenue cyclicality to fall over the next four to eight quarters as pharma and performance materials grow as a share of revenue.
BLISS-GBS synergies expected to show benefit in three to four quarters.
capex_capacity: BLISS-GBS utilisation is in the 40s% and rising, per management.
Multi-purpose plant capacity, kept ready in advance, allowed commercialisation of a new product for a US specialty metal customer within four months, with supplies starting November 2026.
Management said the standalone order book equates to about 6-7 years of revenue on average.
Management said it will look for an API-side acquisition to complete the pharma value chain, but no target has been identified publicly.
Group cash is held across entities; management says it will keep cash in each entity for working capital and small capex, and has not loaded debt onto acquired targets.
demand_pricing: Long-term supply agreements and LOIs total about ₹1,750 crore, per management.
A six-year long-term supply agreement was signed with a leading US specialty metal manufacturer, a new end segment; management did not disclose value or volume.
Management said sulfuric acid prices rose from ₹7 to ₹45 per kg, and the company said it passed through costs while keeping margins stable.
A Japanese customer's volume of about 1,000 tonnes was reportedly expected to triple after J-Hawk's US supply was announced.
Management said there is active CDMO discussion with BLISS-GBS customers, but no quantification given.

qa_highlights.question: Is there progress on acquiring an API business, and on CDMO scaling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is actively evaluating API targets but has nothing to share. CDMO discussions with BLISS-GBS customers are advanced, but nothing quantifiable yet.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 34% standalone EBITDA margin structural, and will guidance be revised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the strong quarter to product mix and urged caution, keeping prior guidance of 24-26%.

qa_highlights.question: What is BLISS-GBS's steady-state margin and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Guided to 22-24% margin, in line with the group's consolidated level; utilisation in the 40s%. Synergies are expected in three to four quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How is the acquisition funded?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹1,450 crore from a non-controlling, non-voting instrument (led by Bain Capital) with a right to buy out later, plus ₹300 crore of term debt at the BLISS-GBS subsidiary level priced in the single digits; no debt servicing burden in the first year.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the US metal manufacturer contract won and what are the volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: The product was developed in four months, commercial supply starts November 2026, and management expects about ₹100-150 crore in FY27 rising significantly after that.

qa_highlights.question: What is J-Hawk's margin improvement plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Process optimisation (solvents, assets, raw materials), better sourcing from India, and effluent treatment cost reduction.

risks_watch: BLISS-GBS is consolidated for only three days in Q2, so H2 revenue depends on full-quarter consolidation.
Working capital cycle remains very high at 271 days.
Management gave limited detail on BLISS-GBS, which is separately listed and does not hold concalls; disclosure visibility is limited.
Acquisition integration and financial controls across recent deals (J-Hawk, BLISS-GBS) need to be proven.
Standalone Q2 revenue fell YoY on the ₹180 crore one-time base effect; the underlying trend is unclear.
Raw-material price volatility (sulfuric acid) against the claim of stable pricing pass-through.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, margins and the strategic rationale, but cautious on guidance: management repeatedly declined to raise standalone margin guidance and withheld quantification on CDMO, API and BLISS-GBS details.
key_quotes: Our consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 25% in Q2 FY 27 compared to 19% in the corresponding quarter last year, while H1 margins improved from 26% from 22%.
I would urge to the caution and continue to guide at the numbers that we have been guiding.

adds.what: BLISS-GBS acquisition completed 28 Sept 2026 (acquired capacity, consolidated 3 days in Q2; utilisation in 40s% and rising)

growth.why: Management guided H2 FY27 consolidated revenue to ₹2,400-2,500 crore (annualised ~₹4,800-5,000 crore) and 20-25% organic growth over 3-5 years, backed by standalone order book/LOIs of ~₹1,750 crore (vs ~₹350 crore last-year standalone revenue) and BLISS-GBS acquisition, though no capacity expansion timelines or numbers were given beyond the acquisition.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin ~25% vs 19% a year ago on performance materials and mix, but management kept standalone guidance at 24-26% and urged caution, and consolidated guidance at 22-24% with BLISS-GBS steady-state margin in that same band.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: BLISS-GBS acquired 28 Sept 2026 and utilisation is in the 40s% and rising, with synergies expected in three to four quarters, so acquired capacity ramps through H2 FY27 without a new build.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H2 FY27 consolidated revenue guided to Rs 2,400-2,500 crore with BLISS-GBS and J-Hawk for full periods, versus H1 total income of Rs 1,489 crore, and standalone order book of about Rs 1,750 crore implies 1.8-2x last year's ~Rs 350 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No new capex guided; management is seeking an API-side acquisition and CDMO discussions are advanced, but no target or quantification has been named.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to raise standalone margin guidance (kept 24-26%) and urged caution on the 34% quarter, though the H2 revenue range is new and above H1 run-rate.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Working capital cycle remains at 271 days, sulfuric acid rose from Rs 7 to Rs 45 per kg, and BLISS-GBS integration and controls are unproven, so H2 revenue delivery depends on full-quarter consolidation.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: New product for a US specialty metal customer starts commercial supply in Nov 2026, expected at Rs 100-150 crore in FY27 per management, with a six-year long-term supply agreement signed.

rows.label: Standalone order book ~Rs 1,750 crore
rows.why: LOIs and long-term contracts of about Rs 1,750 crore equal 6-7 years of revenue, implying standalone revenue of 1.8-2x last year's ~Rs 350 crore this year.

rows.label: US specialty metal customer six-year supply deal
rows.why: Six-year long-term supply agreement signed with a leading US specialty metal manufacturer, a new end segment; value and volume not disclosed, with Rs 100-150 crore expected in FY27.

rows.label: Acquisition funded without debt on acquired targets
rows.why: About Rs 1,450 crore came from a non-voting instrument led by Bain Capital, plus Rs 300 crore of term debt at BLISS-GBS level in single digits, with no debt servicing burden in year one; buy-out right may add later outflow.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, the US contract and the BLISS-GBS rationale but cautious on guidance, declining to raise standalone margin guidance; analysts pushed on whether the 34% standalone margin is structural and on API and CDMO progress, which management did not quantify.
